filename: Spatiotemporal Machine Learning Approaches forAtmospheric Composition Emulation in NASA GISS Model E.pdf
title: Spatiotemporal Machine Learning Approaches for Atmospheric Composition Emulation in NASA GISS ModelE
venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Machine Learning and Computation
parameterization_target: surface-level Black Carbon from biomass burning (BCB) concentration
testbed_rationale: The simulation datasets used for training and evaluating the emulators are not published or linked to an open data repository (only code is archived on Zenodo/GitHub).
pain_points: Autoregressive models (SFNO) suffer from rapid error compounding and divergence without frequent ground-truth re-initialization or physics-based mass/spectral constraints.
Emulators struggle to capture extreme high-concentration events due to dynamic range spanning orders of magnitude, with loss functions biased toward moderate values and zeroing out low values.
Generalization across decadal climate shifts is impaired when normalization parameters from a single historical year (1950) are applied to periods with shifted emission baselines (2010).
Offline emulation is currently confined to surface pressure level; vertical mixing and 3D structure must be added before full online coupling into ModelE's radiative and cloud schemes is possible.
extraction_notes: The study develops 'Smart-NINT' to replace the non-interactive precalculated monthly climatology of aerosol fields in NASA GISS ModelE with an interactive, meteorologically driven spatiotemporal ML emulator.
